summary: Heerlen sets street parking itself: from 1 January 2026 the council tariff is 1.50 euros per hour (raised from 1.00 euro in 2024), with day rates of 3.00 euros on designated long-stay spaces, and a 2026 college decision fixes paid hours and regimes street by street. Resident and business permits are rationed by sector (the 2026 issuing decision caps 2,194 permits against 1,790 spaces in 14 resident sectors, plus 23 business-only permits), run for six months and cost 13.60 euros per month for a first resident permit. The municipality owns almost no garages (a 2015 concept parking note says only one, in Heerlerheide); Q-Park's Heerlen page lists eight facilities with about 3,128 spaces, including the 236-space P+R Parallelweg at the station and 60 charge points across the garages, while Interparking ran the Maanplein and Maankwartier garages in 2019. Council questions in January 2025 show that garage prices (up to 3 euros per hour) rather than street prices shape the image of expensive centre parking, and the coalition agreement promises to make tariffs visible. Retail vacancy at 't Loon is the main demand-side signal found; the only occupancy figures are from a 2018 survey. The municipal website was offline on 21 October 2026, so current municipal parking pages could not be read, and no 2025-2026 plan for new or closed garages or for the P+R was found.

items.text: The council adopted the Parkeerverordening Heerlen 2023 on 31 May 2023, replacing the 2016 ordinance. Permits are issued per plate and per address, for six months, for designated permit-holder places and combi places (paid places that permit holders may also use), and the college may cap the number of permits per sector.
items.source_title: Verordening op het gebruik van parkeerplaatsen en de verlening van vergunningen (Parkeerverordening 2023)

items.text: Published on 1 April 2026 (college decision of 10 February 2026), the Besluit uitgifte parkeervergunningen Heerlen 2026 allows at most two resident permits per dwelling and two per business (one in sectors 108, 220 and 221), one active plate per permit and five plate changes a year. When a sector reaches its cap, applicants go on a waiting list and residents rank ahead of businesses.

The 2026 issuing decision sets a cap of 2,194 permits against 1,790 maximum parking capacity across 14 resident sectors (101-106, 108, 210, 230, 240, 250, 310, 320, 410), i.e. 100 to 140 percent of capacity, plus 11 business permits in the centre (sector 220) and 12 for Willemstraat (221). Sector 230 (Baronstraat/Parallelweg area) is the largest at 660 permits for 550 spaces.

On 10 March 2026 the college fixed the places, times and manner of paid and permit parking (published 1 April 2026). Street regimes include 60 minutes (A1), 120 minutes (A2), whole day (A3-A5) and 15 minutes (A6); paid hours differ by street, for example Monday-Saturday 09:00-18:00 with Thursday until 21:00 and Sundays and holidays 12:00-18:00.

Council decision of 6 November 2025 (Verordening parkeerbelastingen Heerlen 2026, in effect from 1 January 2026): 1.50 euros per hour for street parking in the centre, 't Loon and outside the centre, 3.00 euros per 12 hours on designated long-stay spaces and at Nieuw Eyckholt, 5.40 euros per day on other designated spaces. A first resident permit is 13.60 euros per month (second 17.00), a first business permit 19.90, a penalty charge 82.00 euros.

The council decided on 7 November 2024 to raise street parking from 1.00 to 1.50 euros per hour from 1 January 2025 (3.00 euros per 12 hours on long-stay spaces unchanged). A first resident permit was set at 13.30 euros per month and the penalty charge at 78.80 euros.

L1 reported on 20 December 2023 that Heerlen left its street tariff unchanged for 2024 at 1 euro per hour, the cheapest of the Limburg towns surveyed (Kerkrade 1.50, Weert 1.60, Sittard-Geleen about 1.90, Venlo and Roermond 2.80, Maastricht 3.50).
items.source_title: Maastricht uitzondering met forse stijging parkeertarieven (L1 Nieuws)

items.text: In 2021 the council reduced the street tariff in and outside the centre from 2.00 and 1.80 euros to 1.00 euro per hour for 2022, correcting an amendment that had accidentally kept a free first hour; day tariffs stayed unchanged. The cost was to be covered from the corona budget.

On 20 January 2025 a CDA council member asked written questions saying street parking (1.50 euros per hour, 3 euros per day in many places) is far cheaper than the Q-Park garages (up to 3 euros per hour), that street spaces are heavily occupied, and that the coalition agreement promises to make municipal and Q-Park tariffs visible. This is a question and opinion, not a decision or a college answer.
items.source_title: Schriftelijke vragen Parkeren Heerlen Centrum (20 januari 2025)

items.text: Q-Park's Heerlen page, read on 21 October 2026, lists eight facilities: Corio Center, De Klomp, P+R Parallelweg, Putgraaf, Raadhuisparking, 't Loon, Teleparking and Theater Heerlen Parking. Their pages give 504, 364, 236, 307, 379, 383, 451 and 504 spaces, about 3,128 in total; tariffs did not load in the fetched pages.

On Q-Park's pages read on 21 October 2026, Heerlen garages list 60 electric charge points in total: 't Loon 16, Raadhuisparking 12, Corio Center 8, Teleparking 8, Theater Heerlen Parking 8, De Klomp 4 and Putgraaf 4; none is listed for P+R Parallelweg.

Q-Park's P+R Parallelweg page, read on 21 October 2026, shows 236 spaces, 2.10 m clearance, 24/7 opening, licence plate recognition and a rail-traveller discount for same-day return journeys by train with a different check-out station. Tariffs did not load.

A council information letter of 8 January 2019 listed tariffs at 1 January 2019: Q-Park Corio and Raadhuis 1.00 euro per 24 minutes (day 15.00), P+R Parallelweg 2.32 per hour (day 13.91, NS day rate 4.00), Teleparking and Klompstraat day 9.50; Parking+Protection/Interparking ran the Maanplein and Maankwartier Centrum garages (day 7.50). It counted 4,027 garage and 756 paid street spaces in the centre area. Old figures.
items.source_title: Raadsinformatiebrief Parkeren, evaluatie, tariefdifferentiatie en parkeerproducten 2019

items.text: The municipal parking survey of June 2018 measured an average occupancy of 69 percent (Tuesday 11-12 h) in the centre study area, near 100 percent in the 1-hour A1 zone during shopping hours, about 94 percent in long-stay zone B1 and about 100 percent at Nieuw Eyckholt on weekdays; the target is 50-80 percent. Old figures.

Q-Park's garage De Klomp (Klompstraat) was closed on 5 September 2024 after a car fire the evening before, with customers allowed to drive out; Q-Park awaited a safety report. The L1 article does not state when it reopened.
items.source_title: Parkeergarage Q-Park blijft dicht na brand: situatie onveilig (L1 Nieuws)

items.text: A concept Parkeernota (vision and ambition document) dated 23 November 2015 states that after selling its parking real estate the municipality owns no garages (except Heerlerheide) and steers only street parking. It proposed, as a concept, a study of a P+R at station De Kissel, a multi-year tariff agreement with Q-Park, paid parking on shopping Sundays and gradually setting the street tariff above the garage tariff. Old concept; the 2019 council letter refers to the adopted 2016 version.

A traffic decision published on 4 January 2022 reserved two EV charging bays at the Kloosterstraat/Rietrastraat car park in Hoensbroek (part of Heerlen municipality). It cites the college's 2016 EV charging policy and Heerlen's participation, since 21 July 2020, in the Noord-Brabant public charging-point concession together with the other Parkstad municipalities.

L1 reported on 5 March 2026 that shopping centre 't Loon, which has an underground car park (Q-Park lists a 383-space 't Loon garage at Apollolaan 11), suffers from vacancies, and that its owners want to convert part of the complex into housing. The article says the centre's heyday is over as the number of shopping streets in the centre shrinks.
items.source_title: Vertrek Karnevalswierts zoveelste tegenvaller voor zieltogend winkelcentrum Heerlen (L1 Nieuws)

gaps: heerlen.nl and en.heerlen.nl (parking pages, P+R, station area, Sunday paid parking, mobility policy) returned a 'temporarily unavailable, taken offline for security reasons' notice on 21 October 2026, so no municipal web page could be read.
Q-Park garage and P+R tariffs did not load on the fetched Q-Park pages; centrumparkeren.nl lists tariffs but is a listing portal and was not used.
dichtbij.nl (Cloudflare 403) was not opened and De Limburger was not searched or opened; regional press coverage was limited to L1 Nieuws articles found via its site search.

No parking policy paper newer than the 2019 council letter (mobility vision, parking note after 2016, centre plans, new or closed garages, P+R plans, status of the Interparking Maankwartier/Maanplein garages) was found in opened sources; council answers to the January 2025 questions were not found.
No open-data or parking guidance statement for Heerlen and no recent utilisation figures were found; the only occupancy data read are from the June 2018 survey.
Low-emission or pedestrian zone policy for the centre and the Universiteit Maastricht Promenade plans (L1, 5 November 2025) were not tied to parking in any opened source.
